privacy_001: Effective date: September 30, 2026. AllPlayer is developed by an independent developer and distributed on Apple platforms. This policy explains what information AllPlayer uses when you watch media, connect services, sync devices, or ask for help.
privacy_003: Core playback does not require an AllPlayer account, and we do not sell your personal information. Most app data is handled on your device, by Apple services you enable, or directly between your device and a media source or third-party service you choose.
privacy_007: , we receive your email address and any text, screenshots, diagnostics, or other information you include. Connection-assistant reports are generated on your device for you to review before sharing. We use support information only to respond, troubleshoot, maintain, and improve AllPlayer, and retain it only as reasonably necessary for those purposes or legal obligations.
privacy_009: AllPlayer may access files, Photos items, folders, downloads, disc images, playback history, favorites, watch-later items, settings, and information about your media to provide features you initiate. Local media playback, file management, stream caching, and media-center downloads are handled on your device. We do not operate an AllPlayer media server that uploads or stores your local media files.
privacy_010: Photos access is limited by the permission you grant in system Settings.
privacy_011: Downloads and cached media stay on the device and are not included when viewing progress and library information sync through iCloud.
privacy_012: Local-network transfer or receiver features may make selected content available to other devices that can connect to yours while you enable those features.
privacy_014: When you connect a cloud drive, home server, or remote-access service, AllPlayer saves the address, account details, and sign-in information needed to use it. This lets you reconnect, browse your media, play or download files, and check the connection. Sign-in information is stored using the storage and protection features available on your device. Each service also handles information under its own privacy policy.
privacy_015: Google account and Google Drive data
privacy_016: You can choose to connect Google Drive. With your permission, AllPlayer reads your account name and email address to show which account is connected. It also reads your Drive folders and file details, such as names, sizes, and modification dates, so you can browse your files and play or download media you choose. AllPlayer does not create, change, or delete files in your Google Drive.
privacy_017: AllPlayer saves sign-in information on your device so you can stay connected. This information is not synced through iCloud. If you enable iCloud sync, your connected account name and email, media details, and viewing progress may sync between your devices. Downloaded media and playback caches stay on the device. When you choose to sign in on Apple TV using another device, the sign-in information is encrypted before being sent over your local network.
privacy_018: Google user data is used only to provide the connection, browsing, playback, download and device-sync features you choose. We do not sell this data, use it for advertising or credit decisions, or use it to train generalized artificial intelligence or machine-learning models. We do not permit human access to Google user data except with your affirmative consent, when necessary for security, to comply with applicable law, or as otherwise permitted by Google's Limited Use requirements. AllPlayer's use and transfer to any other app of information received from Google APIs will adhere to the
privacy_019: Google API Services User Data Policy
privacy_022: Account information, file details, and downloaded media remain saved until you remove them. Signing out removes the saved sign-in authorization for that account on the current device. You can also stop AllPlayer from accessing Google Drive through your
privacy_025: Stopping access does not automatically delete downloaded media, cached information, or data already synced to iCloud. You can remove these through AllPlayer and the relevant device or iCloud storage settings. Turning off sync does not delete data already synced; copies on other devices need to be removed separately. For help, or to request deletion of information you sent to us, email
privacy_028: Other cloud drives and NAS services
privacy_029: AllPlayer also supports OneDrive, Dropbox, Box, pCloud, Yandex.Disk, Baidu Netdisk, Quark Netdisk, MEGA, Synology NAS, and fnOS. You choose which services to connect. Depending on the service and permissions you grant, AllPlayer uses account information, folder lists, file names, sizes, dates, and other file details to show your media and play or download the files you choose. Access depends on your account permissions and the service’s restrictions.
privacy_030: AllPlayer saves the connection and sign-in information needed to keep these services available. Some connection information may sync when iCloud sync is enabled, as described below. The service provider handles your sign-in and file requests under its own privacy policy.
privacy_031: You can sign out or remove a connection in AllPlayer. Where the service offers connected-app controls, you can also revoke access in its account settings. Removing a connection does not delete files stored in the original cloud drive or NAS. Downloads, cached information, and previously synced data may remain and can be removed separately through AllPlayer and the relevant device or iCloud storage settings.
privacy_032: iCloud sync and continuing on another device
privacy_033: On supported devices, iCloud configuration sync is on by default. You can turn it off in AllPlayer Settings. It keeps connection settings, stream lists, viewing progress, favorites, and Watch Later available across your devices. For some services, saved sign-in information may also sync; Google Drive sign-in authorization does not. Apple handles synced information under its terms and privacy policy.
privacy_034: Handoff lets you continue supported playback on another device by sharing the information needed to resume. Links containing passwords or sensitive access information, and file locations available only on the original device, are excluded.
privacy_036: When you use an iPhone or iPad to help set up Apple TV, the connection and sign-in information needed for setup is sent over your local network. Supported setup methods encrypt this information before sending it. It is used only for the connection or sign-in you request. Apple Watch exchanges media lists, artwork, playback progress, and control commands with its paired iPhone so you can browse and control playback from your wrist.
privacy_038: AllPlayer uses TMDB to find movie and TV descriptions, posters, and backdrops. Looking up this information involves processing your search terms or the movie or TV item being identified, your language preference, and network information such as your IP address. Video files and cloud-drive sign-in information are not needed for these lookups.
privacy_040: Depending on the features you choose, AllPlayer may communicate with Apple services; cloud, NAS, or media-server providers; Tailscale; OpenSubtitles; TMDB; video or stream hosts; and other sources you configure. These services receive the network and account information necessary to answer your request, including your IP address in ordinary network communication.
privacy_041: If you start an internet speed test, AllPlayer first uses Cloudflare's public speed-test service and may use Measurement Lab (M-Lab) as a fallback. M-Lab retains and publicly publishes measurement data under its privacy policy for Internet research. A remote-server speed test reads data from the selected server and does not upload a test file to it. See
privacy_047: App distribution, purchases, refunds, and purchase restoration are handled by Apple. Apple may also provide crash reports and limited diagnostics such as device model, operating-system and app versions, time of an error, configuration, and crash details according to your device settings. We use diagnostic information only for troubleshooting, reliability, and app improvement.
privacy_049: We do not sell personal information. We share or enable access only as needed to provide a feature you request, use platform and service providers described in this policy, comply with legal obligations, or protect rights and security. We use reasonable safeguards, but no internet, local-network, or electronic-storage method is completely secure.
privacy_051: AllPlayer is not directed to children under 18, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from children. Depending on your location, you may have rights to access, correct, delete, restrict, object to processing, request portability, or withdraw consent for information we control. You can revoke system permissions, disconnect services, turn off iCloud sync, or remove local app data through the app and system Settings. Contact us for requests concerning information you sent directly to us.
privacy_053: We may update this policy as AllPlayer changes. The effective date above identifies the latest published version. For privacy questions or requests, email
support_001: Get setup and troubleshooting help for local playback, NAS and media servers, cloud drives, streams, remote access, casting, and cross-device features.
support_006: Details that help us diagnose an issue
support_008: Include the device model, iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, or watchOS version, and your AllPlayer version.
support_010: Tell us whether the media is on your device, in Photos, on a NAS or media server, in a cloud drive, or from a video link. Include the service name and whether you use Tailscale for remote access.
support_012: Share steps to reproduce, screenshots, visible errors, media format, decoder choice, server type, and whether the same source works on another device.
support_013: Local media or Photos do not play
support_014: Confirm the file is not damaged and that AllPlayer has permission to access the selected file or Photos item. Try both the system and built-in decoder where available. For a file that still will not play, tell us its format, such as MKV or ISO, and what happens when you open it. Include any file details you know.
support_015: A NAS or media server cannot connect
support_016: Check the server address, port, path, username, password, sharing permissions, and firewall. Confirm that the playback device can reach the server network. The connection assistant can discover compatible sources and generate a report you can review before sharing.
support_017: A cloud drive cannot sign in or open a file
support_018: Confirm the provider is available, complete its authorization page, and try signing in again if the sign-in has expired. For Baidu Netdisk or Quark Netdisk, also check account-side playback and download restrictions. See the home page for supported cloud drives and NAS services.
support_020: Check that Tailscale is enabled in AllPlayer and that the connection is authorized. Make sure the device you want to reach is online in the same Tailscale network. Use the address shown for that device in Tailscale, and confirm its file-sharing or media service is running.
support_021: Playback buffers or feels slower than expected
support_022: Use the network tools to test both the current internet connection and the selected server's real download speed. Try a lower stream quality, move closer to Wi-Fi, or compare local-network and remote access. Speed tests are diagnostic only and cannot improve source bandwidth.
support_023: A stream is unstable or caching does not finish
support_024: HLS, m3u8, live, and web video links depend on source availability, authorization, and network quality. Re-add an expired link, select another available quality, and ensure enough local storage is free. Some services or stream formats restrict caching.
support_025: Multi-stream playback or online subtitles are unavailable
support_026: Multi-stream playback supports up to four streams in five layouts and requires Pro access through a purchase or an active trial. For online subtitles, confirm your OpenSubtitles sign-in and network connection; external subtitle matching also depends on the selected media and filename.
support_027: AirPlay, DLNA, or receiver mode is not working
support_028: Keep sender and receiver on a reachable network, allow local-network access, and confirm the receiving feature is enabled. DLNA / UPnP receiving and AirPlay sending vary with the source format; AirPlay receiving is limited to supported iPhone and Mac configurations.
support_029: iCloud, Handoff, Apple TV QR setup, or Apple Watch is not syncing
support_030: Use the same Apple Account where required, enable iCloud and Bluetooth or local-network permissions, and keep the companion devices nearby and updated. Apple Watch browsing and playback control communicate with the paired iPhone; Apple TV QR setup requires both devices to reach the same local network.
support_031: Share import or link analysis fails
support_032: Confirm the source app shared an accessible file or valid link. Some services issue temporary links, require you to sign in through a browser, or prevent third-party access. Share the item again after signing in and do not attempt to save content you are not authorized to access.
